Subject: Renewal planning + capacity uplift request

Hi Soojin,

Hope you had a good week. BlueForge's current commitment (Q4 2025–Q3 2026) is up for renewal at the end of November. We're seeing a 30-40% bump in inference volumes for our recommendations pipeline and need guidance on capacity that keeps unit cost predictable.

Key constraints from procurement:
- We have a fixed renewal budget for Q1; any incremental capacity must either be absorbed within the overall spend or be offset by a credit.
- Legal/procurement need a one-page summary of any exceptions (surge protection, true-up cadence).

Our asks:
1) A renewal structure that lets us ramp (staged uplift) without a full multi-year step commit.
2) Some protection for short-term surges (e.g., 2–3x bursts) without catastrophic overage.
3) One-time onboarding credit for the expanded usage (to offset internal integration costs).

Can you share a concrete proposal and an example pricing ladder? Prefer to have this in the next two weeks so procurement can start paperwork.

Thanks,
Anna Ruiz
Head of Platform Ops
BlueForge

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear note and the RFQ. High level I'm proposing a mixed-commit ladder with a short true-up window and an explicit surge safeguard. Attached is a workbook with two pricing options and sample math. Short summary below:

Proposal (option A — conservative):
- 12-month renewal, base commit = current committed units (no step-up)
- Staged uplift: two scheduled uplift checkpoints (month 3 and month 6) with pre-negotiated uplift tiers (25%, 50%) that can be added with 30 days' notice
- Surge safeguard: 2.5x burst capacity for up to 72 hours/month at capped overage rate (lower than on-demand)
- One-time onboarding credit: $35k credit to offset integration/ingest costs if BlueForge signs by Oct 15
- Discount ladder: larger committed uplift tiers receive incremental discount on per-token price (details in sheet)

Option B (aggressive):
- 18-month term with higher base commit (20% uplift), deeper discounts, smaller onboarding credit ($20k)

Next steps I recommend:
1) Review the attached workbook (SOOJIN-proposal-mixed-commit-v2.xlsx).
2) Confirm whether procurement needs the pricing exposed as monthly or quarterly line items.
3) If Option A looks reasonable I can route a term sheet and a DocuSign for the credit/clause.

I'll hold a short call Thurs to walk through the ladder if helpful — what time works for you?

Best,
Soojin Lee
